budget.rationale: A smoke test, not a result: LLM-SR given the PySR table in time order and sampling at the paper's temperature, through the hosted endpoint, LLM-SR's own evaluator, the recovery of each pick by running it, a development rollout and the sealed result. 400 samples per target (100 requests): in the time-ordered budget pilot the best program read the history by sample 200 and all ten best did by sample 400, so the smoke should seal a pick that reads the history, and show what a two-target cell does.

prompt_policy.description: LLM-SR specifications natively embed a problem description, so supplying the public task specification matches its own protocol.

scope_note: Smoke test on the budget pilot's cell (Dalla Man T1 easy, target Gp) and the two-target Dalla Man T2 hard cell (Gp and I), whose searches run at once and whose task is assembled from both. Its models are never reported.

reasoning_model_adaptation.rationale: LLM-SR was published with models that answer at once. gpt-oss reasons before it answers, within the same token limit, and writes its function header over several lines. Measured on 2026-10-05 by sending this cell's first LLM-SR prompt as a chat message to the hosted gpt-oss-120b, four samples per request: at upstream's 512 new tokens all four stopped at the limit while still reasoning; at 4096 all four finished, at low and at the served default reasoning effort (about 2,200 tokens per sample at the default), but every one split its header, which upstream's reader (sampler._extract_body) takes as the start of the body, so its trimming kept nothing; with the header read as one line, all four were usable, at either effort. Reasoning effort stays at the served default, as upstream sets none; the sampling temperature is the paper's, declared in paper_settings.

regression_table.rationale: LLM-SR fits a function to derivative labels, as PySR does, so it takes the data as our PySR baseline does: the same training rows, the same channels at each row, in PySR's order, and the same labels, numpy.gradient within each trajectory. The rows stay as the table is built: each trajectory in time order, one after another. LLM-SR's programs see whole columns and may read along them. In the budget pilot (T1 easy, time order, 3,532 scored samples) about 85% did, and all of the 100 best: they filtered the meal series to stand in for the unobserved gut compartments. gpt-oss-120b wrote these filters itself; LLM-SR's prompt holds no data, and the model took the time order from the task description. Decided on 2026-10-09: such programs are allowed if they respect causality, and the rows are not shuffled. program_rollout says how a pick that reads the history is run.

program_rollout.rationale: The shared evaluator reads equations of the current values, and a program that reads the history is not one. Such a pick is run as the program it is. Its syntax tree is checked against an allowlist (arithmetic, control flow, helper functions, and listed numpy, math and scipy names); it then runs in a separate process that can import nothing else and write no file, and is killed past its time limit. Its coefficients are refitted with their evaluator's own call, BFGS from all ones on the same table; read without running, the fit was confined to the branches a reader could follow and, in the pilot, settled on other models. Each trajectory is rolled out along its observation grid, uniform within each cell and the same in training and validation, with the trapezoid rule, the program given only that trajectory's rows so far, so a rollout cannot see later rows or another trajectory. A pick that, fitted, is an equation of the current values goes through the shared evaluator, as PySR's do; on the pilot's eight best such picks the two rollouts agreed within 0.3%. Whether a program's output changes when later rows are removed is recorded; how a report treats such a pick is decided before the test data open. Running proposer-written code is otherwise forbidden here (AGENTS.md); this exception for LLM-SR's selected programs was agreed on 2026-10-09, as LLM-SR's own search runs every program it scores.

paper_settings.rationale: The paper (Shojaee et al., ICLR 2025) samples b = 4 skeletons per prompt at temperature 0.8 (Sec. 3.2; App. A: chosen in preliminary experiments), decays the cluster-sampling temperature as T0(1 - (u mod N)/N) with T0 = 0.1 and N = 10,000, and describes e = 4 evaluators (App. A). The code at 41c2123 sends no temperature from its client, so its engine samples at temperature 1 (its API path also sends none); it sets N = 30,000; and it evaluates one sample at a time with any number of evaluators, so e = 4 changes nothing there. Every other setting already matches the paper: k = 2 examples per prompt, 10 islands, a 4-hour reset, a 30-second timeout, 10 parameters fitted by BFGS, and about 2,500 iterations (10,000 samples). The paper's 2 GB memory limit is not in the released sandbox and is not added.
